name: Frobenius theorem: a unit timelike field with u_[a d_b u_c] = 0 is hypersurface orthogonal (the normal of a foliation)

source.located: Frobenius, 'Ueber das Pfaffsche Problem', J. Reine Angew. Math. 82 (1877) 230-315 -- pre-arXiv, NAMED-NOT-READ; Wald (1984) App. B Thms B.3.1/B.3.2 -- book, NAMED-NOT-READ. Read via restatement: (i) Yao, arXiv:2004.07288 (2020, v4 2023) Prop 1.1 p.1-2: the classical theorem exactly, smooth involutive subbundle => LOCAL regular parametrisation near each p; 'a similar theorem also holds for the C^1-subbundles'; Prop 1.11 p.4 Lipschitz version (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007); p.30 'Clearly V is involutive because it has rank 1'. (ii) Ellis & van Elst, gr-qc/9812046 (Cargese 1998) Sec 2.4 p.12: 'When the vorticity vanishes: The fluid flow is hypersurface-orthogonal, and there exists a cosmic time function t such that u_a = -g(x^b) nabla_a t'; p.9 eq (27) non-zero vorticity => 'no 3-surfaces orthogonal to the fluid flow'. (iii) Gourgoulhon, gr-qc/0703035 p.23 (Frobenius for the tangent distribution of a hypersurface, cites Wald Thm B.3.1), p.44 (hypersurface-orthogonal => vanishing vorticity). (iv) Carroll, gr-qc/9712019 p.78 ('known as Frobenius's Theorem ... Let's just take it for granted') and pp.164-165 (closing commutators => integral submanifolds).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2004.07288, gr-qc/9812046, gr-qc/0703035, gr-qc/9712019. No arXiv source was found that prints the twist form u_[a nabla_b u_c] = 0 verbatim; the equivalence of the twist form with (a) involutivity of ker u and (b) the Ellis-van Elst zero-vorticity form is MACHINE-CHECKED here (C4) rather than read.

published_statement: Yao arXiv:2004.07288 Prop 1.1 (restating Frobenius 1877): 'Let M be an n-dimensional smooth manifold and let V be a smooth subbundle of TM with rank r ... Suppose V is involutive. Then for any p in M there is a neighborhood Omega ... and a smooth regular parameterization Phi(u,v): Omega -> M such that Phi(0)=p, and ... dPhi/du^1 ... dPhi/du^r form a basis of V_Phi(u,v)'; 'a similar theorem also holds for the C^1-subbundles with C^1-regular parameterization'. Ellis-van Elst gr-qc/9812046 p.12: 'When the vorticity vanishes: 1. The fluid flow is hypersurface-orthogonal, and there exists a cosmic time function t such that u_a = -g(x^b) nabla_a t'. For V = ker(u) of a nowhere-zero 1-form u, involutivity <=> u ^ du = 0 <=> u_[a nabla_b u_c] = 0 (C2, C4 here).
published_hypotheses: u (equivalently the codimension-1 distribution ker u) nowhere vanishing -- automatic for a unit timelike field

REGULARITY: smooth (Frobenius 1877 as restated), or C^1 (classical extension), or Lipschitz with a.e./set-valued involutivity (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007, restated in 2004.07288 Prop 1.11); log-Lipschitz with distributional involutivity (Yao 2020 Thm 1.4)
LOCALITY: the conclusion is a neighbourhood of each point (u = f d tau on that neighbourhood); a global time function whose level sets are the leaves is NOT asserted
manifold C^1,1 or smoother; torsion-free connection when the condition is written with nabla (so nabla may be replaced by partial derivatives)

later_literature.ref: Yao, arXiv:2004.07288 (2020; v4 2023), The Frobenius Theorem for Log-Lipschitz Subbundles
later_literature.what: Frobenius holds for log-Lipschitz subbundles with distributional involutivity, giving a C^{0,1-eps} parametrisation, and the regularity is sharp (Prop 6.3, X = (1, y log|y|)). Restates the classical smooth/C^1 theorem and the Lipschitz one (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007) and leaves the Osgood case open (Problems 6.5-6.7). It confirms that the conclusion is local and that a regularity hypothesis is part of the theorem.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: Frobenius's theorem (1877; Deahna 1840 and Clebsch 1866 earlier) is a theorem of differential topology. It has NO numerical input and NO measured datum, so there is nothing its authors could have lacked in M's sense, and nothing that could later have moved. Evidence either way: (a) later work (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007, Yao 2020, the 2025-26 papers) only EXTENDS the theorem to weaker regularity. None of it contradicts the smooth/C^1 statement, and the log-Lipschitz sharpness result (Yao Prop 6.3) marks where regularity starts to matter; (b) the one place the tree outruns the source is not missing data but a dropped regularity hypothesis ('w arbitrary'), SHOWN here by the non-Lipschitz counterexample (C7). That hypothesis does not reach any dependent. So having every datum now available leaves the conclusion as used unchanged.
grade_evidence: The theorem, in the form the dependents use, STANDS. (1) Twist condition: re-derived. V5's 0/64 reproduces, and it generalises to any 1-form of (t,r) on any warped product. (2) Twist form <=> zero vorticity <=> involutive ker u: machine-checked (C4). (3) Frobenius's conclusion, tau with d tau ∝ u' and a diagonal adapted chart: constructed numerically for smooth w on Schwarzschild to about 1e-9. The grade is NARROWED and not STANDS only because the tree's prose drops two of the source's hypotheses. REGULARITY: 'For ANY rapidity field w(t,r)' (:105), 'w arbitrary' (:111), 'EVERY SPHERICALLY SYMMETRIC UNIT TIMELIKE FIELD' (:113) is false for continuous non-Lipschitz w. C7 exhibits a spherically symmetric unit timelike u' that is the normal of no foliation, because three leaves pass through (0, c). The true class is w in C^1, or Lipschitz. LOCALITY: :116-118 omits 'locally', and C8 exhibits the adapted chart failing to extend. The narrowing does NOT move any dependent. Ledger D2, specthm D2/K0/R1 and the 'every value realised by a foliation' at :144 need one smooth w per point value and a local foliation, which the theorem provides. This is recorded as a discrepancy of scope in the prose, not an error in the tree's computation, which is itself C^1 (sympy Function). Nothing was repaired.
what_would_change_the_grade: -> STANDS: foliation.py's sentences at :105/:111/:113/:116 read as restricted to C^1 (or Lipschitz) w and to a neighbourhood of each point. The in-file computation already assumes this. -> WRONG: a C^1 spherically symmetric unit timelike field with nonzero twist, or one that is not locally a foliation normal. C2 proves none exists (the twist vanishes identically for every differentiable A(t,r)dt + B(t,r)dr), and classical Frobenius then gives the local foliation. -> OPEN: none; the result is checkable here and was checked.
